surface: one process-global table (dict) of immutable bundles; payloads are private copies isolated from producing and consuming rows (publish-side AND restore-side copies)

measured_on_smoke_shapes.probe: python one-off on tests/execution/fixtures via the public Add* path with UNA_PREPARED=1 (command recorded in git history; figures below are tool output)
measured_on_smoke_shapes.reading: payload size ~= the decoded layer itself (arrays + WKB-equivalent geometry bulk); per-consumer restore copies are the same order again per served row, which is what the produced path allocated anyway (fresh decode per row)

laws_as_implemented_in_B.immutable_leases: payloads are written once at publish (post-success) and never mutated afterwards; bundles are only replaced, never edited
laws_as_implemented_in_B.per_consumer_copies: every served array/GeoSeries/GeoDataFrame is a fresh copy (PP02 asserts `is not` against the previous row AND the lease payload)
laws_as_implemented_in_B.budget_respect: the worker-local table is UNBOUNDED in this increment by design: batch cohorts are bounded row sets and the payload is the decoded layer; growth policy/eviction under live leases is increment C's PP09 duty. No execution.memory_limit_bytes accounting is claimed yet — claiming it without a mechanism would be a false receipt
laws_as_implemented_in_B.no_pointer_transport: worker-local only: nothing crosses a process boundary; geometries travel as live GeoSeries within the process (stage-cache WKB discipline remains for the disk store); derived sindex rebuilt per consumer (PP02/asserted via stage-cache equivalence and query parity in increment A)
laws_as_implemented_in_B.measurement_duty: cohort-shape payload measurements (the 32-job observed cohort) are due with the P05/P03 measured runs; smoke-shape figures above establish the scaling law (payload ~ decoded layer), not the cohort figure
